transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-09-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Alex (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Blueline ML), Jonah (Blueline SRE), Rita (Blueline PM)

Summary: 
Quick sync on the INT8/FP8 runs from last week, surface-level quality deltas, and a short focused run to expose latency spike causes. Action items and a canary plan at the end.

Topics:
- Week-over-week quality delta across eval suites (NLG + classification prompts)
- Latency spikes under burst traffic and KV-cache warmup behavior
- Heuristic tuning (layerwise scale adjustments) and fallback routing
- Next steps: 2k prompt bake, canary, and security checklist items

--- Transcript ---
00:00:01 Maya (AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll wait another minute for folks to trickle in, but wanted to start with a quick status. We ran the INT8 and FP8 blends the last 48 hours, Alex, do you want to kick off with the headline numbers?
00:00:31 Alex (SE): Yeah, sure. So top-line, the INT8 baseline — uh, in-t eight — dropped average throughput a little but reduced token cost about 2.3x. FP8 had slightly better quality preservation on the NLG suite but latency p95 increased by roughly 12%. Those are rough numbers off the initial run.
00:01:02 Priya (ML): Quick clarifying Q — when you say p95, are we looking at our Aurora test instance with the 512 window or the 1k? Because that matters.
00:01:14 Alex (SE): Good point. These were the 512 context runs, single stream, no KV cache priming. We did a limited 1k run later that's in the spreadsheet but less samples.
00:01:27 Samir (SE): Also note that the FP8 build was on the latest microkernel; INT8 used an earlier kernel that is slightly faster for MatMul in our rig. We need a matched kernel comparison.
00:01:45 Jonah (SRE): From an infra perspective the p99 spikes we saw align with cold KV-cache fills, the first 50 tokens post-request had a 3x latency variance. So warmup and batching thresholds mattered.
00:02:08 Rita (Product): Is that the thing we could mask with a short-term coalescer? Or would that increase tail for everyone?
00:02:17 Alex (SE): The coalescer helps throughput but can bump median a bit. There's a trade there. For this pilot, we suggested heuristic gating: if request tokens < 128 then route to non-batched low-latency pool; else batch.
00:02:34 Priya (ML): On quality delta — we ran Rouge, BLEU-ish style for the generative prompts, and an F1 macro for classification. INT8 shows systematic hallucination in rare-entity prompts (financial entities especially). FP8 retained them 95% of the time. There were some label mismatches though; our eval harness is a bit noisy.
00:03:05 Maya (AE): When you say hallucination, can you give an example?
00:03:09 Priya (ML): Yeah, prompt id DF-229 — asks for quarterly tax treatment for a UK subsidiary — INT8 sometimes invents a tax code, FP8 gives the blanker or cites the parent doc.
00:03:25 Alex (SE): That smells like a precision underflow in the low-rank projection layers. We tried a per-layer scale tweak that recovered a chunk of those cases — about 60% improvement on that sub-sample.
00:03:40 Priya (ML): Did you try a fallback tie-breaker? Like run INT8 then cheaply re-rank with the FP8 candidate?
00:03:48 Samir (SE): We did a short re-rank test; cost doubles for those requests, but if you only re-rank when confidence score < 0.6 it's tolerable. The throughput drop is limited to roughly 6% of traffic.
00:04:06 Jonah (SRE): Are those confidence scores stable under quantization? If the metric itself is biased by the quant noise then we'd mis-fire.
00:04:16 Alex (SE): Right, the score distribution shifts with quantization, we need calibration. We can produce a small calibration sweep — map confidence thresholds from FP32 to INT8/FP8 so the trigger is meaningful.
00:04:29 Rita (Product): Timeline check: we need a pilot that won't blow up the SLA. Can we document expected fallback rates and cost impact?
00:04:39 Maya (AE): Yes, we'll deliver a waterfall chart by next Thursday. Alex, can you scope the calibration run and waterfall?
00:04:46 Alex (SE): Yep, 2k prompts, run INT8, FP8, and an FP16 baseline, compute per-prompt delta, calibration map, and a proposed tie-breaker latency/cost trade table. That'll take us 48 hrs.
00:05:02 Priya (ML): Example-level diffs will be super helpful. Also, can you include the tokenizer boundary cases? We noticed different tokenization led to token count variance under INT8 which affects the batch scheduler.
00:05:16 Samir (SE): Good call — we'll annotate tokenization deltas; sometimes the tokenization pushes short prompts into the coalescer threshold, then delay shows up.
00:05:27 Maya (AE): Quick note on security/compliance: Jonah flagged egress keys and rotation windows for the private pilot. Jonah?
00:05:35 Jonah (SRE): Yeah, for private we need KMS integration and a 48-hour PKI rotation window during which we can't do major deploys. Also, audit logs need to be pulled into our SIEM; is that supported out of the box?
00:05:49 Alex (SE): Redwood provides audit logs; for Private we can export to S3 (or your syslog) with per-request metadata. We'll share the export config.
00:05:58 Rita (Product): For exec readouts, Rita here, what's the bottom-line latency delta if we do the heuristic routing vs straight FP8?
00:06:07 Alex (SE): Heuristic routing keeps median roughly the same as FP16 baseline, INT8 gives best cost but more tail. FP8 sits in the middle; with routing we can keep p95 within SLA for 95% of traffic. We'll quantify in the charts.
00:06:22 Priya (ML): Another question — were any of the regressions correlated with specific layers or attention heads?
00:06:29 Samir (SE): Early signs point to two projection layers in the middle block; we ran a per-layer clip/scale that fixed some hallucination. We'll include a sensitivity heatmap in the artifact.
00:06:42 Priya (ML): Great, the heatmap will help our model team prioritize. Also, can you include a recommended quant config for experiments on GCP A2? We're running some tests there.
00:06:52 Alex (SE): We'll add a variant tuned for NV-arch vs the Aurora benchmark; call out kernel differences.
00:06:58 Maya (AE): Switching gears — latency exposure plan, Jonah, you mentioned cold KV fills. What's your proposed mitigation timeline?
00:07:06 Jonah (SRE): Short term: warmup priming for high-probability endpoints, sticky small cache for first 100 tokens. Medium: pre-warm by replaying representative prefixes during low traffic windows. Long: move to prefix-aware caching in the serving runtime.
00:07:22 Maya (AE): We can help with a prefix sampling job and include the KV warm traces in the report.
00:07:29 Priya (ML): One more practical: how will we decide canary thresholds? We need both quality and latency triggers.
00:07:36 Alex (SE): Proposed triggers: quality delta > 3% aggregate F1 drop on the classification suite OR p95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline. Canary abort if either persists after 24 hours at 5% traffic.
00:07:50 Rita (Product): That seems reasonable. Can you put that in a one-pager?
00:07:53 Maya (AE): Yup, will include in the canary SOP.
00:08:00 Priya (ML): Noise in transcription: sorry, tiny sidebar — some of our examples are PII, can we mask them in the CSV?
00:08:07 Maya (AE): Absolutely; we'll mask and include the original context hashes for traceability.
00:08:12 Samir (SE): Quick interruption — I just saw a weird outlier in the INT8 1k run where GPU utilization plummeted. Could be kernel mismatch or scheduling thrash. We'll investigate.
00:08:23 Alex (SE): Related — we need to run matched-kernel INT8 vs FP8, otherwise we're comparing hardware/driver differences too.
00:08:30 Jonah (SRE): I'll open a ticket with infra with the kernel/driver versions and attach our perf traces.
00:08:36 Maya (AE): Perfect. Any other blockers?
00:08:40 Priya (ML): We need the per-prompt diffs and the 5-10 worst-case examples tagged with why they fail — hallucination vs omission vs tokenization — that will help our labeling.
00:08:53 Maya (AE): Noted.
00:09:00 Alex (SE): Logistics — we'll push the 2k run overnight and share artifacts in the drive link. Also, we'll run a small re-rank cost sim for the tie-breaker and show expected cost impact at 5% fallback rate.
00:09:15 Priya (ML): Thanks. On routing, can you recommend default thresholds we can try on prod at low traffic?
00:09:22 Alex (SE): Default: token_threshold 128, confidence_threshold 0.6 after calibration mapping, batch_window 15ms for the coalescer. We'll include a recommended YAML snippet.
00:09:33 Rita (Product): And docs for SSO and audit?
00:09:36 Maya (AE): We'll share the security pack post-call — SSO/SAML, KMS integration, retention options.
00:09:42 Jonah (SRE): One ask: we want RBAC role mapping to our AD groups; can Redwood map service user roles to groups?
00:09:50 Alex (SE): Yes, SAML mapping supports group assertions; we'll document exact claim names.
00:09:57 Maya (AE): Cool. Any final quick notes?
00:10:02 Priya (ML): Nothing else. Thanks folks.
00:10:05 Maya (AE): Okay, recap of next steps: 2k prompt run, waterfall + per-prompt CSV, calibration mapping, canary SOP one-pager, infra ticket for kernel match, and Blueline will share labeled failure examples. We'll reconvene next week same time.
00:10:22 Alex (SE): I'll post the drive link and a short README.
00:10:26 Maya (AE): Perfect, thanks everyone. Meeting end.

Note: transcript includes occasional mis-heard tokens and speaker label artifacts; timestamps approximate.
